messages.subject: IMPORTANT!! Rkoholik beginner's course announcement
parts:
PLEASE READ THROUGH THE E-MAIL EVEN IF YOU ARE AN ADVANCED USER, AS WE WILL NEED YOUR HELP!

Dear Rkoholiks,

At the advanced user's meeting on Wednesday, we finalized the details for the previously discussed beginner's course of our favorite software package (R, of course). So, these are the conclusions, and "rules of the game" both for lecturers and participants:

We decided that the curriculum would follow the online book of Andrej Blejec. It has everything that's needed to learn R, is not as scary as the Crawley book, and is freely available on the Internet.

The sessions will be held every two weeks, on Wednesdays, at 16:00.

All lessons will be "hands on", meaning that you will get to work directly through the study material. Each session should last approximately 2 hours. They will be organized into two parts: first, the topic will be explained (but the participants get to work through the explanation on the computers), and second the participants get assignments they try to complete, and get help if/when they run into problems. We're also discussing follow-up homework assignments that would be provided in an e-mail during the week when there are no lessons. In this manner the participants would have a chance to run into their own problems, and solve them at the next session. This homework, however, will depend on the time the person organizing a lesson has available and may not happen after each session.

So, this is the schedule proposed so far:

20. 1. 2010 - Chapter 3: How to start (with R)
4.2.2010 - Chapter 4: Objects and data structures
18.2.2010 - Chapter 4: Objects and data structures
4.3.2010 - Chapter 5: Data import/export
18.3.2010 - Chapter 9: Plotting (graphs)

This schedule will be updated as we go along. There are currently five people ready to prepare lessons: Roman, Maarten, Tomaz, Martin and Prof. Blejec (we wish him a speedy recovery from his accident). Later, in May, Pina and Luka will also be joining the lecturers. We also hope that as many advanced users as possible will be available in each session to help with problems. Also, if anyone else is willing to participate as a lecturer, he or she is VERY VERY WELCOME!

Technically, all meetings will be held in the computer lab (B6) at the Biology Department, Večna pot 111. There is a number of computers available there, but it would be appreciated if you also bring your own laptops if you can. We will provide and open Wi-Fi network at each session so that you can connect to the Internet and with other computers.

Each lecturer will announce his/her lecture a week before the session, and provide the required material (data files etc.) for the people that bring their own laptops to best use the course time (so that we don't run around with USB sticks). The lecturer will also be responsible for the follow-up homework (at his/her discretion).

The first lesson will be prepared by Roman. He'll send the details shortly.

Hope to see you all there next week!

Cheers,

Maarten and Tomaz
